account:
It is day 1, six in the morning. Today I have my normal appointments, including the mill grain inspection at ten, and an approved civic presentation of thanks in the great hall from eighteen hundred to eighteen thirty. The secretary and innkeeper have both stressed that preparations will finish at eighteen hundred and that I should not arrive earlier. I should buy a writable book for the secretary this morning so the appointment can be recorded in a supplement, then read my appointment book at the office.

There has been unusual activity around bread and preparations. Yesterday freight carried bread into the great hall. The secretary could not confirm what it was for. Near the inn I saw the builder give planks and a lantern to the baker, and heard them confirm these materials were full payment for forty-four loaves, replacing an emerald arrangement. The baker promised delivery but declined to tell me the occasion or destination, calling it a private customer order. The innkeeper was busy and said my presence at eighteen hundred was all they needed.

My best guess is that the innkeeper, builder, baker, and perhaps freight are arranging refreshments and decorations for today's presentation, possibly keeping some of it a surprise for me. The secretary is handling the official appointment, but I do not know how much else the secretary knows. I have not established that the forty-four loaves or the bread freight carried are connected to the presentation, nor do I know their delivery arrangements. The coordinated preparations and repeated requests not to arrive early make a surprise celebration plausible, rather than proof of some unrelated secret business.
